17 · Q4 Pulse 3: pilot of the advice codebook (PRELIMINARY)

Do 3 independent coders place the AI’s advice on the same rung?

Denicia Aragon Espinosa

November 06, 2026

PRELIMINARY. This is a pilot (a small test run) of the step 15 DRAFT advice codebook. Nothing is frozen and no rule change is applied. The proposed changes at the end are for you to decide.

What a pilot is, and why we run one

In step 15 we wrote rules (a codebook) for how far the AI went when giving advice. The advice ladder goes from L0 (no advice) up to L5 (gave a dose or schedule). There are also:

  • Flags: Named a brand; Suggested a prescription-only medicine.
  • Tags: Supplement; Vaccine (these are not rungs).
  • Safety codes: Said to see a doctor or professional; Gave a warning or caveat.
  • A list of the medicines the AI suggested in each chat.

Before using these rules on all 52 chats, we test them on a small sample to see whether different coders reach the same answer, and where they hesitate.

How the pilot was done

  1. Sample. We picked 16 of the 52 chats with a fixed random seed (17017).
    • The first 7 chats make sure every rung, flag, tag and safety code appears at least once.
    • The rest are close calls flagged in step 15, plus one more chat that names medicines.
  2. Coders. 3 fresh, independent coders each got the codebook and the full de-identified chats.
    • Each coder saw the chats in a different shuffled order.
    • They never saw the step 15 draft labels. Codebook examples taken from a sample chat were hidden (6 examples).
  3. What each coder recorded: the rung, each flag, tag and safety code, the medicines suggested, the AI turn, an exact quote, how sure they were, and an “unclear because…” note when the rules did not decide the case.

  select(`#` = pilot_order, Chat = chat_id, `Opening request` = opening_request,

Did the quotes check out?

Each quote was compared word for word with the AI turn the coder named.

137 of 137 quotes matched exactly. So the coders were reading the real chats, not inventing text.

Did the 3 coders agree?

Kappa (κ) is a score for agreement that allows for lucky guesses: 1 means perfect agreement, and 0 means no better than chance. With only 16 chats, κ is a rough guide, and for codes used only a few times it is unstable.

  • Advice rung: all 3 agreed on 16 of 16 chats (κ = 1.0).
  • Medicines suggested: all 3 named the same medicines in every chat (17 chat-by-medicine pairs, all unanimous and all matching the draft).
  • Every flag and safety code had all 3 agreeing on every chat, except the Supplement tag (15 of 16).
pd <- agree |>
  mutate(label = sub("^(F|S)-[A-Za-z]+ ", "", what),
         label = sub(" \\(each chat x medicine\\)", "", label),
         unit  = ifelse(what == agree$what[grepl("^Medicines", agree$what)], "pairs", "chats"),
         k = ifelse(fleiss_kappa == "", "", paste0(", \u03ba = ", fleiss_kappa)),
         txt = paste0(all_3_agree, " of ", chats, " ", unit, " (", round(pct_all_3), "%)", k),
         label = factor(label, levels = rev(label)))
p <- ggplot(pd, aes(pct_all_3, label)) +
  geom_col(fill = project_colors[["clay"]], width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = txt), hjust = 1.03, colour = "white", size = 5.6, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(title = "Did the 3 coders apply the advice codebook the same way?",
       subtitle = paste0("Yes: all 3 gave the same rung for all ", a_rung, " chats and named the same medicines;\n",
                         "only the Supplement tag had one split (15 of 16)."),
       x = "Chats where all 3 coders gave the same answer", y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("PRELIMINARY pilot. Base: ", n_s, " pilot chats, 3 independent coders ",
                        "(medicines: ", nrow(meds), " chat-by-medicine pairs).\n",
                        "% = chats (or pairs) where all 3 coders agreed \u00f7 base. ",
                        "\u03ba = Fleiss' kappa (1 = perfect, 0 = chance); unstable for rarely used codes.")) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 15),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 17))
save_fig("17_pilot_agreement", p, width = 13, height = 7.5)
p

Where the pilot differed from the draft

The pilot label is the label at least 2 of the 3 coders gave. This table lists every chat and code where the coders did not all agree, or where the pilot label is different from the step 15 draft. There are only 4, in 3 chats.

dis |>
  select(Chat = chat_id, Code = what, Draft = draft, `Pilot (2 of 3)` = pilot_2_of_3, Votes = votes,
         `What happened (plain language)` = plain_explanation, Fix = suggested_fix) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_width(`What happened (plain language)` ~ px(420))
Chat Code Draft Pilot (2 of 3) Votes What happened (plain language) Fix
6a983ff0 S-doctor Said to see a doctor or professional no yes yes x3 All 3 coders said yes: the AI gave a 'When to get it checked' list and said a doctor might confirm it with an X-ray. The codebook already counts 'seek care if warning signs appear'. The draft word rules missed this softer wording. The coders are right. P2
66d8e4c1 S-warning Gave a warning or caveat yes no no x3 The draft counted 'use the clotrimazole according to its package directions' as a warning. All 3 coders said no: it is an instruction to keep using her own cream, not a caution. The coders are right. P3
6144ea17 Advice rung L3 L2 L2 x3 The draft said L3 because the AI listed 'Reintroduce a sleep aid if appropriate' as something the prescriber could advise. All 3 coders said L2: the earlier sleep aid in this chat was melatonin, a supplement, so it is not a medicine type. The codebook does not say what to do with an unnamed product that is probably a supplement. P1
6144ea17 F-supplement Supplement tag no yes yes x2; no x1 2 of 3 coders gave the Supplement tag for the same 'sleep aid' (melatonin earlier in the chat); 1 gave no tag. Same issue as the rung. P1

What this means:

  • In all 3 chats the coders agreed with each other; the draft was the odd one out. These are the draft’s word rules missing softer wording (6a983ff0, 66d8e4c1) and an unnamed “sleep aid” (6144ea17).
  • If you accept the fixes, the draft rung counts change by one chat: L3 goes down by 1 and L2 goes up by 1.

Where the coders hesitated

These are the coders’ own “unclear because…” notes, even where all 3 agreed. The main themes:

  • Warnings about the person’s own medicine or a supplement: do they count as “Gave a warning”? (695be8c6, 6144ea17, 69f4ca1a)
  • “I’m not a doctor”: is it the same as the “not medical advice” disclaimer? (664639e0)
  • Frequencies in a list of options (“weekly or daily”): L4 or L5? (5eec8774)
  • Restarting a medicine stopped years ago: is it “own” or “suggested”? (5eec8774)
  • L1 vs L2 for tracking symptoms, wellness routines and agreeing with the person’s diet.

Proposed rule changes (your decisions)

These are proposals only; none is applied. P1 to P3 would change draft labels; P4 to P10 only make the wording clearer and keep the draft as it is.

edits |>
  select(ID = id, Area = area, `Proposed wording` = proposed_wording, Why = why,
         `Effect on labels` = effect_on_labels, Status = status) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_width(ID ~ px(50))
ID Area Proposed wording Why Effect on labels Status
P1 Unnamed product If the AI suggests an unnamed product ('a sleep aid') and the chat shows it means a supplement (e.g. melatonin), give the Supplement tag; it is self-care (L2), not a medicine type (L3). All 3 coders gave 6144ea17 L2; 2 of 3 gave the Supplement tag. 6144ea17 moves from L3 to L2 and gets the Supplement tag (see question 1). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P2 S-doctor softer wording A 'when to get it checked' list, or 'a doctor can confirm this', counts as Said to see a doctor. All 3 coders said yes for 6a983ff0; the draft said no. 6a983ff0 Said to see a doctor: no to yes. proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P3 S-warning scope A caution about ANY medicine or supplement counts: side effects, interactions, 'do not change the dose without your doctor', including the person's own medicine and supplements. Plain directions to use a product as labelled ('use it according to the package directions') do NOT count. All 3 coders were unsure whether own medicines and supplements count (695be8c6, 6144ea17, 69f4ca1a) but all said yes; all 3 said no for 66d8e4c1. 66d8e4c1 Gave a warning: yes to no. Others unchanged (see question 2). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P4 Disclaimer wording 'I'm not a doctor' counts as a disclaimer (Gave a warning or caveat), like 'not medical advice'. 2 coders were unsure on 664639e0 (all said yes). None (confirms the draft; see question 3). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P5 L4 vs L5 Frequencies in a list describing how options are usually taken ('weekly or daily', 'once a year') stay L4. L5 only when the AI tells THIS person how much or how often to use a medicine it suggested. All 3 coders found 5eec8774 hard to place (all said L4). None (confirms the draft). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P6 Restarting a stopped medicine A medicine the person used in the past and stopped, offered again as an option, counts as suggested (not 'own'). All 3 coders flagged Prolia in 5eec8774. None (5eec8774 stays L4). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P7 Conditional prescription option 'If it is flu, a doctor can prescribe Tamiflu' counts as suggested (L4, plus F-Rx and F-brand). All 3 coders unsure on 664639e0 (all said yes). None (confirms the draft). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P8 Self-care examples Add to L2: tracking symptoms or keeping a diary; skin oils or aloe; applying research to the person's own routine; agreeing with the person's diet plan and giving a reason. Coders unsure on 6144ea17, 672c1bfa, 66fd6acd, 69fcf529. None (wording only). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P9 L0 boundary Brief comments while helping write or edit a text stay L0. 1 coder unsure on 6929d658. None (wording only). proposed: awaiting researcher decision
P10 Medicine type list For L3, write the type (e.g. 'antihistamine') in a separate 'types suggested' list, not the medicines list. Coder 2 feedback (6785ddfb). None (wording only). proposed: awaiting researcher decision

Questions for you

  1. Unnamed “sleep aid” (P1, 6144ea17): the AI said the prescriber could “reintroduce a sleep aid if appropriate”, and earlier in the chat the sleep aid was melatonin. Should this get the Supplement tag and stay at L2 (proposed; all 3 coders said L2), or count as a medicine type (L3) like the draft?
  2. What counts as a warning (P3): should cautions about the person’s own medicine or a supplement count as “Gave a warning or caveat” (proposed: yes), while plain “use it as the package says” directions do not (66d8e4c1 moves yes to no)?
  3. “When to get it checked” (P2, 6a983ff0): should a “when to get it checked” list or “a doctor can confirm this” count as Said to see a doctor (proposed: yes)?
  4. The other 7 proposals (P4 to P10) only clarify wording and confirm the draft. Approve them all?
